title: The BEZERU Blueprint: How We Judge Watches
excerpt: The lens we use to review modern and vintage watches—design, ergonomics, and what actually matters on the wrist.
content: Welcome to BEZERU. This is the lens we use to judge watches: proportion, ergonomics, and honest design decisions.
We start with how the watch wears: lug-to-lug, thickness, crown comfort, and bracelet taper.
Then we look at design: dial typography, index proportions, and whether the watch has a coherent identity.
Finally: movement decisions—because engineering choices always show up in the design.

title: Vintage Lens: The Quiet Genius of Seiko Moonphase Dress Watches
excerpt: A calm complication done right: why Seiko moonphase dress pieces feel timeless—and how to buy them well.
content: Moonphase watches have a reputation for being loud. Seiko proved the opposite: restrained case shapes, clean dials, and complications that feel like part of the design—not decoration.
When you hunt these, condition matters more than hype: look for sharp cases, clean printing, and honest service history.
The best examples feel like design objects—quiet, wearable, and surprisingly modern.

title: Release Radar: 5 Watches Worth Your Time This Week
excerpt: A fast scan of what’s new—what changed, what’s marketing noise, and what’s genuinely interesting.
content: This week’s releases prove a pattern: the biggest improvements are often the least photogenic—thinner cases, better taper, sharper dials.
We’re watching for real design progress: legibility, proportion, and the details you notice after three months of wear.
